Michael Saylor: Digital Credit Is Our Product, MSTR Is Just a Byproduct

On October 20, 2026, Michael Saylor explained in an interview with Schwab Network that Strategy converts Bitcoin into dividend-paying digital credit products to meet the cash flow needs of a different group of investors. He said supporting these products' prices and bringing them back to par allows the company to continue issuing them and command a premium to net asset value, which is why Strategy uses capital to buy back preferred stock. If the credit business doesn't work, Strategy is simply a Bitcoin holding company. — link

S&P Global acquires OpenZeppelin to boost digital asset risk capabilities

S&P Global has completed its acquisition of blockchain security firm OpenZeppelin for an undisclosed amount. The deal is intended to strengthen S&P Global’s digital asset and smart contract risk capabilities. OpenZeppelin will continue to operate independently under founder Demian Brener, while its open-source smart contract libraries will remain freely available. — link

Galaxy: Bitcoin bear market ended in June, accumulation phase underway

Galaxy Research said Bitcoin’s bear market ended in June 2026 and the asset is now in an accumulation phase, with BTC closing above its 50-week moving average for five consecutive weeks. Monthly transfers from coins held for more than five years have fallen to about 34,000 BTC from 67,000 in 2024, suggesting reduced selling pressure from long-term holders. Galaxy said the bullish view would weaken if Bitcoin falls below its roughly $76,540 50-week moving average and fails to reclaim it within a month. — link

Keystone Breach Exposed 25,964 Purchase Records and Compromised Device Verification Key

Keystone said its latest investigation found that attackers obtained a WebAuth device-authentication key through the website breach, potentially allowing counterfeit hardware wallets to pass official authenticity checks. The company will destroy 18,835 unsold devices using the old key, pause unshipped orders and switch new production to a replacement key. The incident also affected 25,964 purchase records and 12,873 incomplete checkout records, while Keystone said seed phrases, private keys and transaction signing were not compromised. — link

Akash Network selects Solana for blockchain migration

Akash Network said it has selected Solana as the destination for its planned blockchain migration. The decentralized GPU and AI compute network currently runs its own Cosmos SDK-based chain, but previously said it intends to move to a shared-security architecture to reduce network maintenance costs and the capital burden associated with AKT staking. Solana and Ethereum had both been under consideration before Akash made its final choice. — link

Jack Dorsey's Bitcoin-Enabled Bitchat Tops France's App Store Social Chart

Jack Dorsey's decentralized messaging app Bitchat topped France's App Store Social Networking chart following nationwide protests and an Orange network outage on October 21. The app enables offline messaging via Bluetooth mesh networks, supports Nostr-based communication, and integrates Bitcoin-backed Cashu eCash payments. — link

Ethereum Delays Glamsterdam Hoodi Fork Over EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 Risks

Ethereum researcher Toni Wahrstätter said the planned Glamsterdam fork on the Hoodi testnet has been delayed after ChainSecurity identified compatibility risks in EIP-8037 and EIP-8038. The gas changes could break contracts that assume gas usage only decreases or cause failed sub-calls to behave unexpectedly. ChainSecurity has found 13 real-world cases, and developers are reviewing whether the upgrade specification needs changes. — link

Hyperliquid: Kraken Parent Payward Plans to Become First CFTC-Regulated HIP-3* Deployer

Hyperliquid announced that Kraken parent Payward plans to become the first CFTC-regulated HIP-3* deployer, using Hyperliquid infrastructure to offer perpetual futures markets to U.S. clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Payward's CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, Bitnomial, would serve as the deployer, managing the markets and clearing and settling contracts, while its CFTC-registered FCM, NinjaTrader Clearing, would carry client accounts. HIP-3* will introduce optional onchain allowlists for permissioned markets without affecting existing HIP-3 markets. The initial version is available on testnet, with specifications subject to change. — link
